nfl.oneThing: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is on track to start against the Bears on Sunday despite a rib injury, coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday, as long as there are no setbacks this week.

headlines.title: Penix on track to start for the Falcons
headlines.summary: Penix took a big hit late in Sunday night's home loss to the Ravens and came out of the game, returning one play later. When the game went to overtime, Tua Tagovailoa entered, and his interception ended it after the Ravens scored on their first OT drive. Penix took all the first-team reps on Wednesday and was listed as a full participant. Stefanski wouldn't go into detail on the imaging, and Penix said the results were positive.
headlines.whyItMatters: Atlanta are 2–3 and one game behind the NFC's seventh seed, so keeping Penix healthy matters for their playoff chances.

headlines.title: Simmons back in practice, Mahomes full for the Chiefs
headlines.summary: Left tackle Josh Simmons was officially limited in his return to practice on the Chiefs' Wednesday injury report. He hasn't played all season while dealing with a back injury, and undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has filled in. Patrick Mahomes was a full participant despite his knee. Rashee Rice didn't take part to start the week, and L'Jarius Sneed was limited.
headlines.whyItMatters: Kansas City are 4–0 and top of the AFC, so the left tackle position is the one to watch as Simmons builds back up.

headlines.title: Gonzalez ready to return for the Patriots, Brown back in practice
headlines.summary: Christian Gonzalez, who has missed the past two games with a shoulder injury, said he's 'ready for Sunday' against the Jets. He watched New England's 45–17 win over the Raiders from the sideline. A.J. Brown was a limited practice participant, his first practice since going on injured reserve on Sept. 12, and the Patriots have designated him to return from injured reserve.
headlines.whyItMatters: New England are 3–2 and fifth in the AFC, so having Gonzalez and Brown back helps their push for a playoff spot.

headlines.title: Cowboys still short of healthy bodies at 2–3
headlines.summary: Dallas are 2–3 after losing to the Buccaneers last Thursday. DeMarvion Overshown has been out since the season opener and didn't practise, and Cobie Durant was a DNP. Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) was limited, while CeeDee Lamb and Tyler Guyton were full participants. The Cowboys face the Packers in another primetime game this week.
headlines.whyItMatters: A report says Dallas are only one game behind in the win column for the NFC East lead, so every healthy player counts.

teamNews.title: Carter Runyon's 21-day practice window opens
teamNews.text: The Raiders designated tight end Carter Runyon to return from injured reserve on Wednesday. They can activate him at any point in the next three weeks. He went on IR on Aug. 30 with an undisclosed injury and became eligible to return last week after missing four games.

teamNews.title: Nailor sits out practice with concussion
teamNews.text: Receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not practise on Wednesday, according to Sam Warren of The Athletic. He is listed as questionable for Sunday.

teamNews.title: Silver and Black Pride previews the Bills
teamNews.text: Buffalo are 4–1, and the preview says Josh Allen has seven touchdown passes and eight rushing touchdowns this season. James Cook has run for at least 111 yards in three of the Bills' five games, and the Raiders have had trouble stopping the run at times.

nba.oneThing: Kristaps Porziņģis will remain out indefinitely with the Warriors because of a 'health-related matter', about a week before Golden State's regular-season opener against the Lakers.

headlines.title: Porziņģis to remain out indefinitely for the Warriors
headlines.summary: The Warriors announced that Kristaps Porziņģis will remain out indefinitely because of a 'health-related matter', but he will stay around the team. He missed training camp and Golden State's first five preseason games. He returned to the team's practice facility on Wednesday. Porziņģis posted that he is 'working with doctors and experts' and 'getting better and better', but it's still unclear what he is dealing with.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Warriors open the regular season in Los Angeles against the Lakers in about a week, with no timeline for their 31-year-old big man.

headlines.title: Podziemski's five-year extension gets a fan verdict
headlines.summary: The Warriors reached an agreement on a five-year, $110 million extension with fourth-year guard Brandin Podziemski. It starts with the 2027-28 season, so he will play out this year on the final season of his rookie-scale deal. SB Nation Reacts calls it a middle-of-the-road extension that pays him like a quality starter, not a star. The site is asking Warriors fans to grade the deal.
headlines.whyItMatters: It's a long-term commitment to a young guard, and the fan reaction will show how the Warriors' core is viewed.

headlines.title: Redick says Bronny James hasn't played well in preseason
headlines.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick said he doesn't think Bronny James has played well in the preseason. James has combined for 11 points and 12 turnovers in four games. Redick said the struggles don't tell the full story. His explanation drew attention, with one headline describing it as throwing Lakers teammates under the bus.
headlines.whyItMatters: The regular season is less than a week away, so the Lakers' rotation questions will be answered soon.

headlines.title: Toronto's rise puts the East's top four in focus
headlines.summary: ESPN's Perk calls Kawhi Leonard the 'most feared' and most dangerous player in the East. The Raptors won 46 games last year, their most since 2021-22, and finished fifth in the East. They then pushed the fourth-seeded Cavaliers to the brink in the first round of the playoffs. Leonard had 21 points and five rebounds in Toronto's preseason win over the Knicks.
headlines.whyItMatters: Last year's 46-win season sets a high bar, and the question now is whether the Raptors can finish in the East's top four.

teamNews.title: Spurs' defensive depth
teamNews.text: Air Alamo writes that the Spurs' defensive depth punishes teams with limited shot creation. Yahoo Sports says Tarris Reed Jr. gives them what they were missing last season.

recaps.text: Austin Reaves did most of the scoring for the Lakers with 28 points and seven assists, but Golden State's balance was enough. Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski shared the Warriors' scoring load, and Stephen Curry contributed quietly.

recaps.keyLine: Avdija 26 pts, 9 reb, 4 ast · Lillard 14 pts, 3 reb, 4 ast · Mogbo 15 pts, 10 reb, 4 ast · Newton 15 pts, 2 reb, 3 ast
recaps.text: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant added to the scoring, and Portland improved to 3–0. The Kings are 0–4 and missing big men Dylan Cardwell and Maxime Raynaud, both out with injuries. Jonathan Mogbo and Precious Achiuwa gave Sacramento some inside production.

recaps.keyLine: Haliburton 24 pts, 3 reb, 3 ast · Zubac 13 pts, 13 reb, 5 ast, 3 stl · McCain 20 pts, 2 reb, 2 ast, 6 3PM · Williams 16 pts, 4 reb, 3 ast
recaps.text: Oklahoma City needed overtime to beat Indiana in a close finish. Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac were the Pacers' main contributors, with Zubac's rebounding and steals keeping them within reach.

recaps.keyLine: Thomas 16 pts, 3 reb, 0 ast · Mitchell 15 pts, 2 reb, 8 ast · Banchero 24 pts, 8 reb, 3 ast · Wagner 20 pts, 4 reb, 8 ast
recaps.text: Orlando pulled away from Cleveland and took the win. Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner were Orlando's main scorers, with Wagner also dishing out eight assists. Donovan Mitchell had eight assists for the Cavaliers, but Cleveland couldn't keep pace on the scoreboard.

recaps.keyLine: Wiseman 18 pts, 10 reb, 0 ast · Diawara 13 pts, 3 reb, 1 ast · Leonard 21 pts, 5 reb, 0 ast · Barnes 19 pts, 6 reb, 4 ast
recaps.text: Toronto were far too good for New York, winning by a wide margin. Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles all scored at least 19 points for the Raptors.
